items.name: admin-theme
items.title: Admin theme
items.description: Admin colors and radii, including a pair of success and warning tokens on top of the standard shadcn set, for both light and dark schemes. Installed first: the rest of the admin-kit items rely on these tokens.

items.name: admin-shell
items.title: Admin shell
items.description: The admin's permanent frame at full viewport height: an optional header, a side navigation, and a work area with its own scroll — the sidebar and its footer stay put while the content scrolls. Navigation is a single tree node: on a wide screen it's a sidebar with the app name and section labels, on a narrow one the same node becomes an icon rail by styling alone, never swapped for a different node. The controlled collapsed prop collapses the sidebar to that same rail on a wide screen too, and a burger with a panel appears there — the collapsed view on a wide screen behaves just like on a narrow one, differing only by the collapse button; the consumer holds the state. The sidebarVariant prop switches the look: card (default) is a separate panel with rounding and inset, flush sits against the screen edge. The header prop turns the header off entirely, and then on a narrow screen the burger moves to the top of the sidebar. The sidebarFooter slot lives at the bottom of the sidebar and in the burger panel, and the shell — not the content — controls its layout. Nav items support icons and swapping the link render for your own router; an item without an icon shows the first letter of its title when collapsed, and the accessible name stays the section title. The burger panel remounts on every open, so slot content must be controlled from the outside — the same rule the whole kit lives by. Requires the admin-theme theme.

items.name: theme-toggle
items.title: Theme toggle
items.description: A theme-switch button with no knowledge of how the theme is stored: the isDark state and the onToggle handler arrive as props, and there's neither next-themes nor a context of its own inside. The icon shows the state a click will switch to, and the screen-reader label changes along with it. Fits both the shell's sidebarFooter slot and a standalone spot on a page.

items.name: sidebar-toggle
items.title: Sidebar toggle
items.description: A button that collapses the shell's sidebar into an icon rail on a wide screen, built like theme-toggle: the collapsed state and the onToggle handler arrive as props, with no state of its own. The icon shows the action a click will perform, and the screen-reader label changes along with it. Hidden on a narrow screen right inside the element itself — there the sidebar is already an icon rail with a burger, so the button isn't needed. Its place is the shell's sidebarFooter slot next to the theme toggle; no dedicated prop for it is needed in admin-shell.

items.name: language-toggle
items.title: Language toggle
items.description: A locale-switch button with no knowledge of where the locale is stored, built like theme-toggle: the current locale, the list of available locales, and the onLocaleChange handler arrive as props, with no i18n library and no context of its own inside. The button shows the short label of the current locale (e.g. "EN"), falling back to a Languages icon before the current locale is known, and a click cycles to the next locale in the list, wrapping back to the first. Fits the shell's sidebarFooter slot next to theme-toggle or anywhere else on the page — it holds no internal state, so it renders identically in every sidebarFooter instance.

items.name: user-menu
items.title: User menu
items.description: An avatar icon button for the shell's sidebarFooter slot that opens a dropdown with the signed-in user's name, email, and a list of actions — profile, sign out, and similar. The fallback avatar shows initials derived from name (the first letters of its first two words, uppercase); avatarUrl swaps in a real image. An item's tone="danger" colors it with the destructive color, matching row-actions. The dropdown's open state lives in the primitive, same as every other popup in the kit — that's transient UI state, not the persistent state the sidebarFooter contract warns about, so it doesn't break the slot's multi-instance mounting.

items.name: breadcrumbs
items.title: Breadcrumbs
items.description: A trail of section links above a page's heading. Every entry except the last renders as a link when it has an href (through renderLink when provided, a plain <a> otherwise — the same substitution pattern as admin-shell's renderLink); an entry without an href in the middle of the trail renders as plain text. The last entry is always the current page — BreadcrumbPage with aria-current="page", never a link, regardless of whether it has an href. Server-compatible: no client state, no "use client".

items.name: locale-ru
items.title: Russian locale pack
items.description: A Russian dictionary for the kit's items: a single const, localeRu, sliced into the exact shapes the other items' labels and locale props expect, so a slice spreads or passes straight into a prop — labels={localeRu.widgetTable}, locale={localeRu.dateField.locale}. Covers widget-table, widget-list, widget-chart, state-loading, state-error, state-forbidden, state-offline, widget-placeholder, confirm-dialog, date-field, date-time-field, color-field, sidebar-toggle, theme-toggle, admin-shell, language-toggle, user-menu, and breadcrumbs, and bundles date-fns's ru locale for the date fields. Not a runtime i18n solution — it's a static dictionary, and switching locale at runtime is on the consumer.

items.name: widget-metric
items.title: Metric widget
items.description: A single-number card for a dashboard: title, value, an optional trend with an arrow, and a caption. direction sets the arrow, and a separate tone prop sets the color (derived from direction by default). Data is passed as props. Requires the admin-theme theme.

items.name: widget-table
items.title: Table widget
items.description: A self-sufficient table card: the title is optional, the header holds a toolbar slot for filters on the left and a record count, page-size select, and sort select on the right, and the footer holds centered pagination. A column pulls its value from the row via cell and aligns with the align prop; a column with sortable gets a sort button in its header and aria-sort. The sort select is set with a sortOptions list, and an option's key need not match a column: this lets you sort by a field that isn't rendered, or apply a composite sort behind one opaque key. Sorting and paging are controlled: the table reports the choice via onSortChange and onPageChange but never reorders or slices the rows itself — whoever owns the data sets the order and the slice, otherwise the element would lie on a server with paginated output. With no rows and no empty prop of its own it shows state-empty; the header and footer stay in place. Passing both selectedKeys and onSelectionChange adds a checkbox column: the header checkbox selects or clears every row on the current page only, and once a row is selected it swaps the left side of the header for a selection bar showing an N-selected count, the selectionActions as small buttons, and a clear button.

items.name: widget-chart
items.title: Chart widget
items.description: A chart card for a dashboard: a shared labels axis and a series list, each with its own values — the values length must match labels, or the missing points simply aren't drawn. The kind prop switches the rendering between a line (default) and bars. Series color comes from the chart-1…chart-5 tokens in order; past five series the colors cycle, and two series of the same color on one chart read as a bug. The legend appears only when there's more than one series. With no labels or no series at all it shows the "No data" state. Requires the admin-theme theme.

items.name: widget-list
items.title: List widget
items.description: A list of rows for a dashboard: a title, an optional description under it, an optional meta on the right, and an optional icon on the left. The icon is accepted as a component — the element doesn't pull in a specific icon library. With no rows and no empty prop passed it shows StateEmpty with "No data". Requires the admin-theme theme.

items.name: widget-placeholder
items.title: Widget placeholder
items.description: A dashed frame with muted text marking a spot in the work area where a widget hasn't been chosen yet. It doesn't show a "no data" state — widgets already have a built-in StateEmpty for that; this placeholder is about the widget itself being missing, not about data being missing inside it. Both texts are optional and default to English. Requires the admin-theme theme.

items.name: state-loading
items.title: Loading state
items.description: A skeleton in place of content while data is on its way. The row count is set by a prop, and role=status and aria-busy are set for screen readers. Requires the admin-theme theme.

items.name: state-empty
items.title: Empty state
items.description: The screen a user sees in place of content when there's no data: a title, an optional description, and an optional actions slot. No data is normal, so there's no icon by default. Requires the admin-theme theme.

items.name: state-error
items.title: Error state
items.description: A screen for a loading or request failure: a title, an optional description, and an optional actions slot, with an error icon by default — the failure should read before the text does. Not for missing data — state-empty covers that. Requires the admin-theme theme.

items.name: state-forbidden
items.title: Forbidden state
items.description: A screen for access denial: a title, an optional description, and an optional actions slot, with a muted lock icon by default — lacking permissions is a denial, not a breakage, so the color isn't alarming. Requires the admin-theme theme.

items.name: state-offline
items.title: Offline state
items.description: A screen for a lost connection: a title, an optional description, and an optional actions slot, with a network-disconnect icon by default — the failure should read before the text does. Not for a server error — state-error covers that. Requires the admin-theme theme.

items.name: page-entity
items.title: Entity page
items.description: A single-record page: a title with actions on the right and fields grouped into sections. A field's value is a ReactNode, not a string: links, badges, and amounts with their own formatting live alongside the text. A section without a title is allowed — for an unnamed header made of the main fields. The status prop swaps the fields for one of the loading, error, forbidden, or offline states, while the title stays visible. No forms, no editing: edit buttons live in actions. Requires the admin-theme theme.

items.name: page-header
items.title: Section header
items.description: A page title, an optional description under it, and an actions slot on the right. A building block for every admin page, not a dashboard widget. Requires the admin-theme theme.

items.name: status-badge
items.title: Status badge
items.description: A record-status badge: an order is new or cancelled, a product is in stock or out, a user is active or blocked. The tone is set by the tone prop (neutral, success, warning, danger) rather than derived from the text. The success and warning colors come from the admin-kit theme's tokens of the same name — the standard shadcn set doesn't have them, so the element requires the admin-theme theme and colors incorrectly without it. A building block for a page, not a dashboard widget.

items.name: admin-toaster
items.title: Toast notifications
items.description: Toasts about an operation's outcome: an order was saved, an email failed to send, stock is running low. AdminToaster is placed once — in the root layout or in the shell — and shows nothing by itself; toasts are triggered by calling notify.info, notify.success, notify.warning, and notify.danger from anywhere in the code, including handlers outside React. The element has no state or context of its own: the queue lives in the toast primitive's manager. The tone sets the whole toast's color — the same tokens as status-badge: neutral dark for info, success, warning, and destructive for the rest — and its icon; optional description and an actionLabel/onAction pair add explanatory text and an action button inside the toast.

items.name: confirm-dialog
items.title: Confirm dialog
items.description: A confirmation dialog for an action — delete a record, cancel an order, revoke access. Controlled: the consumer holds open and onOpenChange, and closing it after success is on them too, so the dialog can be left open while a request is still in flight. The tone prop colors the confirm button (default, or danger for an irreversible action), and loading disables both buttons, shows a busy indicator, and blocks closing via Escape or an outside click. Button labels are set by props, defaulting to "Confirm" and "Cancel".

items.name: hint
items.title: Hint
items.description: A tooltip hint for a field label, column header, or metric: it explains a term or what goes into a figure, without taking up screen space. With no children it draws a muted question-mark icon whose accessible name comes from text; with children it wraps the passed element with its own trigger and draws no icon. The side prop picks which side it pops up on, and the render prop swaps in your own element instead of the default trigger — this lets you hang the hint on an existing button instead of nesting a button inside a button. The trigger is a native button, so the hint also opens from the keyboard; TooltipProvider isn't required, it only syncs the delay between neighboring tooltips.

items.name: row-actions
items.title: Row actions
items.description: A row of compact icon buttons for a table row or a list card: view, edit, delete. The label takes up no space in the row but remains the button's accessible name and pops up as a tooltip on hover — the element reuses hint for that. The danger tone colors the icon with the destructive color, and disabled blocks an individual action. Controlled: each action gets its own onSelect, and the element holds no state of its own.

items.name: date-field
items.title: Date field
items.description: A single-date picker with a calendar in a popover. The value is a YYYY-MM-DD string, and an empty string means "nothing selected": there's no Date object and no timezone in the props — parsing and formatting go by local date components, so the value never drifts a day off during serialization or on the server. Controlled: the consumer holds value and onChange. The trigger button, as wide as the field, shows the date in English (e.g. "August 10, 2026"), and picking a date in the calendar closes the popover right away. The label prop draws a caption and links it to the trigger.

items.name: date-time-field
items.title: Date-time field
items.description: A picker for a date together with a time. The value is a YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm string with no seconds and no timezone, and an empty string means "nothing selected". Controlled, built like date-field but deliberately independent of it: registry items are installed one at a time, so each one parses its string on its own. The popover has a time field next to the calendar — changing the date keeps the chosen time, changing the time keeps the date, and if there's no date yet, today is used. The popover doesn't close when a date is picked, or there'd be no time to set the time.

items.name: time-field
items.title: Time field
items.description: A time picker built on a native input type=time: the value is an HH:mm string in 24-hour format, and an empty string means "nothing selected". Controlled, holds no state of its own. The step prop sets the step in minutes (5 by default) and is converted to seconds internally, as the native element requires; min and max constrain the selection in the same format. The native base is a deliberate choice — it gives keyboard input, a local format, and a mobile picker with no code of your own; the clock icon is inverted in the dark theme.

items.name: color-field
items.title: Color field
items.description: A color picker for entities that carry their own color — an order tag, a product category, a kanban column. The value is a HEX string like #rrggbb, and an empty string means "nothing selected"; the color always leaves the component in lowercase. Controlled. Inside the popover: a grid of quick colors from presets (its own palette of twelve data colors, not theme tokens — otherwise the value stored in the consumer's database would shift along with the look), a native input type=color for an arbitrary shade, and a text field for manually typing a HEX code, where an unfinished entry never leaves as a value.

items.name: text-field
items.title: Text field
items.description: A single-line text input. The value is a string; the type prop switches between text, email, password, url and tel. Renders label, control, hint and error in the kit's shared field anatomy: when error is set it replaces the hint, the control gets aria-invalid and aria-describedby. Controlled: the consumer holds value and onChange.

items.name: number-field
items.title: Number field
items.description: A numeric input. The value is deliberately a string and passes through unparsed — mid-typing states like "1." or "-" cannot live in a number, and the kit's field values stay serializable; the consumer parses on submit. min, max and step forward to the native input. Renders label, control, hint and error in the kit's shared field anatomy: when error is set it replaces the hint, the control gets aria-invalid and aria-describedby. Controlled: the consumer holds value and onChange.

items.name: textarea-field
items.title: Textarea field
items.description: A multi-line text input with a rows prop (4 by default). The value is a string. Renders label, control, hint and error in the kit's shared field anatomy: when error is set it replaces the hint, the control gets aria-invalid and aria-describedby. Controlled: the consumer holds value and onChange.

items.name: select-field
items.title: Select field
items.description: A single-choice select over an options list of value/label pairs. An empty value shows the placeholder ("Select…" by default — the placeholder prop localizes it); the popup is pinned to the trigger like the kit's other selects. Renders label, control, hint and error in the kit's shared field anatomy: when error is set it replaces the hint, the control gets aria-invalid and aria-describedby. Controlled: the consumer holds value and onChange.

items.name: checkbox-field
items.title: Checkbox field
items.description: A boolean checkbox with its label to the right; hint or error render below the pair. Controlled via checked and onChange. Renders label, control, hint and error in the kit's shared field anatomy: when error is set it replaces the hint, the control gets aria-invalid and aria-describedby. Controlled: the consumer holds value and onChange.

items.name: page-form
items.title: Form page
items.description: A create/edit record page: a header with a title, description and an actions slot, sections of consumer-laid-out fields, and a footer with Cancel and Save (labels are props, so they localize). It is a real form element — Save submits, submitting disables both buttons and sets aria-busy. The status prop (ready/loading/error/forbidden/offline) swaps the sections for the matching State screen while the header stays. Requires the state screens it renders.

items.name: widget-progress
items.title: Progress widget
items.description: A progress-bar card for a dashboard: warehouse fill level, plan completion, quota usage. Next to the bar is a percentage share computed against max (100 by default). A value outside the range doesn't break the layout: a negative one counts as zero, one above max counts as the maximum. Requires the admin-theme theme.

items.name: page-list
items.title: List page
items.description: A list page: a section title, optional actions, a filter bar, a table, and pagination underneath it. Everything is controlled: the page stores neither the current page number nor the filter values, it receives them as props and reports changes via onFilterChange and onPageChange. The status prop picks the body's content: loading, error, forbidden, and offline swap in the matching state, ready shows the table; the title and filters stay visible under any status, so the request can be retried with a different filter. Pagination is built from page, pageSize, and total, and isn't rendered at all if total isn't passed. A filter is either a text search or a dropdown list. Row selection forwards straight through to widget-table, the same way sorting and pagination do: pass selectedKeys, onSelectionChange, and selectionActions and the underlying table renders the checkbox column and selection bar. Requires the admin-theme theme.
